architecture.mechanism: A difficulty-aware simulator synthesizes instances across a spectrum of difficulty levels (easy, moderate, hard) — using a modified GAN for moderate samples and a "Copycat" that imitates the classifier's behavior for hard examples — so the system is exposed to real-world diversity and its response to unknown, unpredictable inputs becomes predictable rather than erratic.
architecture.intervention: Apply this to the 2019 Silverado 1500 transmission control module (TCM) calibration/validation pipeline by building a difficulty-aware shift simulator that generates acceleration and shift events across difficulty levels — easy (normal torque, smooth road load), moderate (high load/tow/grade, partial clutch slip) and hard (unknown anomalous states: torque converter shudder, driveline resonance, clutch apply-pressure deviation at 40–60 mph) — with a Copycat-style nominal-response model that imitates the transmission's healthy shift behavior and flags deviations as unknown states, then re-tuning shift scheduling, line pressure, and torque converter lock-up strategy against the full difficulty spectrum.
architecture.expected_effect: The TCM becomes robust to previously unknown anomalous operating states during acceleration, detecting and counteracting vibration and shift difficulty (via line pressure, shift timing, converter lock-up adjustments) without requiring a warning indicator to illuminate, because the hard-difficulty vibration regimes were already simulated and calibrated for.
architecture.falsification_test: On a hardware-in-the-loop transmission test bench or vehicle, run the difficulty-aware simulator to inject easy/moderate/hard acceleration-shift scenarios including induced shudder at 40–60 mph; the mechanism is falsified if the Copycat-based nominal-response detector fails to identify the vibration state, or if a TCM calibrated on the difficulty spectrum does not measurably reduce vibration and shift difficulty versus a baseline calibration never exposed to the simulated difficulty range.
